description: A debt-capital-markets director must authorize and structure a proposed commercial-paper issuance, deciding the amount, maturity, investor eligibility, and execution commitments with input from liquidity risk, investor coverage, and legal.

shared_context.S1: The company has proposed issuing commercial paper to fund seasonal inventory purchases.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary term sheet proposes a $40,000,000 issuance with a 90-day maturity.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the issuance and set its final terms.
shared_context.S4: Under the desk's normal pre-launch routine, Elena asks liquidity risk, investor coverage, and legal to report any constraints or execution requirements before authorizing the issue.
shared_context.S5: Elena's authorization record must identify each newly reported constraint or confirmed requirement that changes a final term, cite its source, and assign the affected desk an execution or documentation commitment before the issue can launch.

PF1.text: Malik confirmed in this morning's liquidity stress review that internal policy caps commercial paper maturing within 90 days at exactly $25,000,000; the updated limit has not yet been entered in the issuance dashboard.

PF2.text: Hannah received investor confirmations this morning for exactly $25,000,000 of 180-day commercial paper from existing institutional accounts, but the confirmations have not yet been circulated to the deal team.

PF3.text: Victor found in the current securities-law opinion this week that the notes may be issued only to qualified institutional buyers and must carry a qualified-institutional-buyer legend; this has not yet been added to the term sheet.

acceptance_conditions: The issuance amount must be exactly $25,000,000.
The commercial paper must have a maturity of exactly 180 days.
The notes must be restricted to qualified institutional buyers.
A qualified-institutional-buyer legend must be attached.
The settlement must include an investor-coverage allocation, confirmation, placement, or equivalent execution commitment.
The settlement must include a legal documentation or condition-precedent commitment that addresses the qualified-institutional-buyer legend.

content_checks.C6: any(c.get('target') in ['investor coverage desk', 'Investor Coverage', 'Hannah', 'Hannah / Investor Coverage', 'trading desk', 'issuance desk'] and c.get('type') in ['execution', 'documentation', 'investor_allocation', 'investor_confirmation', 'investor_placement', 'investor_confirmation_circulation', 'condition_precedent'] and ('investor' in c.get('detail', '') or 'subscription' in c.get('detail', '') or 'allocation' in c.get('detail', '') or 'placement' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c.get('target') in ['legal desk', 'Legal', 'legal', 'Victor', 'Victor / Legal'] and c.get('type') in ['execution', 'documentation', 'documentation_update', 'term_sheet_update', 'qualified_institutional_buyer_legend', 'condition_precedent'] and ('qualified-institutional-buyer' in c.get('detail', '') or 'qualified institutional buyer' in c.get('detail', '') or 'QIB' in c.get('detail', '') or 'legend' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The public term sheet proposes $40,000,000, while PF1 changes issuance_amount_usd to the exact $25,000,000 policy maximum and supplies the risk basis that must be cited.

Without PF2, the proposed 90-day issue has no confirmed buyer support; PF2 changes the viable approval to exactly $25,000,000 with a 180-day maturity and requires an investor-coverage execution commitment.
The preliminary term sheet has no investor-eligibility restriction or legend, while PF3 changes both decisions to true and requires a legal documentation commitment addressing the QIB legend.
